---

🚀 Amazon SDE-2 Interview Experience

Interviewed for the Amazon SDE-2 role in April.
After clearing the OA, I was invited for 5 interview rounds (face-face).

Sharing a brief overview to help others preparing 👇
🧪 Round 1 – Data Structures & Algorithms
Design an efficient solution to find the top-K frequent elements from a large dataset.
Approach:
Used HashMap for frequency counting + Min Heap to keep top-K elements.
Time: `O(n log k)`, Space: `O(n)`.

🧪 Round 2 – Problem Solving (Graphs / Trees)
Find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) in a binary tree.
Approach:
Used DFS recursion, returning node when match found and bubbling results upward.
Focused on edge cases (null nodes, same inputs).

🧪 Round 3 – Low Level Design (LLD)
Design a parking lot system.
Approach:
Defined entities (`Vehicle`, `ParkingSlot`, `Ticket`), used OOP principles, enums, and basic extensibility.
Discussed scalability and edge cases.

🧪 Round 4 – High Level Design (HLD)
Design a URL Shortener.
Approach:
Covered APIs, database schema, hashing vs encoding, scalability, collision handling, and caching (Redis).

🧪 Round 5 – Behavioral (Leadership Principles)
Focus Areas:
* Ownership
* Bias for Action
* Handling conflicts
* Failure & learning

**Tip: STAR format is mandatory. Interviewer drilled deep into decisions and trade-offs.

### 📌 Final Verdict

After completing all rounds, the result was shared as “Not Hired”.
No specific feedback or reason was provided, which is standard for Amazon.

Grateful for the learning experience. Back to improving and moving forward 💪

If this helps someone preparing for Amazon SDE-2, feel free to like or share.

[Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) Interview Experience – Round 3 (LLD Round) 🚀

Round 3 at [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) for SDE2(L5) was a Low Level Design (LLD) interview, and it was a deep dive into how you think, not just what you code.

The primary problem discussed was designing Splitwise. The discussion covered:
• Designing core entities (User, Group, Expense, Transaction)
• Maintaining and updating user balance sheets
• Handling different expense types (equal, exact, percentage)
• Validating balances and ensuring correctness of calculations
• Discussing algorithms to keep balances minimal and consistent
• Trade-offs, edge cases, and extensibility of the design

What stood out in this round was the focus on clarity of thought:
• How cleanly you model real-world problems
• How well you justify design decisions
• How you evolve the design step by step instead of jumping to code

The interviewer was less interested in perfect syntax and more interested in:
✔️ Object modeling
✔️ Responsibility separation
✔️ Correctness & scalability
✔️ Communication of ideas

This round reinforced one key lesson for me:

Good LLD is about simplifying complexity while keeping the system flexible for future changes.

Hope this helps anyone preparing for [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) / FAANG LLD rounds.

Happy to share resources and preparation tips—feel free to comment or DM 🙌

🧩 My [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE-2 Interview Experience —

A lot of people asked me about how the actual interview process went, so here is a clear breakdown of my [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE-2 interview journey.
Sharing this to help anyone preparing for [FAANG+](https://linkedin.com/company/faang-plus) or similar product-company roles. 🚀

1️⃣ Online Assessment (OA)
Content:
✔️ DSA questions
✔️ Behavioural section based on Leadership Principles
This was to evaluate both coding fundamentals and decision-making mindset.

2️⃣ Screening Round (DSA)
Focus: Priority Queue based problem
This round mainly tested depth of problem-solving, edge cases, and code quality.

3️⃣ Data Structures Round (DSA – Deep Dive)
Focus: Tree-based problem
Interviewer went into complexity analysis, optimization, and approach clarity.

4️⃣ Low-Level Design (LLD)
Task: Design a complete version of StackOverflow
Covered:
– Class design
– Data modeling
– Core flows (post, comment, vote, moderation)
– Extensibility & clean abstractions

5️⃣ High-Level Design (HLD)
Task: Design an Orchestrator Layer
They went deep into:
– System components
– Scaling concerns
– Async workflows
– Fault tolerance
– Trade-offs
Plus scenario-based Leadership Principle discussions.

6️⃣ Bar Raiser Round
Focus:
✔️ DSA
✔️ Leadership Principles
✔️ Past experience — ownership, impact, complex challenges
This round checked consistency, clarity, and long-term thinking.

🔔 Result: OFFER MIL GYA 🎉
Every round tested a different dimension — coding, design depth, ownership mindset, clarity of thought, and how you handle ambiguity.
If you’re preparing for similar roles, focus on:
🔹 Strong fundamentals
🔹 Structured thinking
🔹 Real ownership stories
🔹 Clear explanations and trade-offs
🔹 Calm mindset during hard follow-up questions

🔥 [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE II Interview. Two months. 1 Assessment. 5 interviews.

🧑💻 My [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) SDE II interview journey. Did I make it?

It started with a simple [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/company/linkedin) message by an [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) Recruiter and ended with a 4-round loop interview🔄.

📌 Step 1: 30-min recruiter screening call
➡️Keep your profile sharp and active on [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/company/linkedin), that’s how I got noticed.

📌 Step 2: Online coding assessment (2 questions, 90 minutes)
➡️Practice timed problems. Ninety minutes disappears faster than you think. Ensure that you cover all edge cases.

📌Step 3: Technical Interview round — 1 coding + 1 behavioral
➡️Be ready for both coding and leadership principles, [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) blends the two.

🎯 Step 4: Final Loop — 4 interviews (2 SDE III,1 Bar Raiser, Hiring Manager)
➡️ Mix of coding, behavioral, and system design, follow-up questions.
Make sure you prepare really well and impress each interviewer with your technical and behavioural aspects.

💯 Make sure you use STAR format while answering the behavioral question, keep your stories handy, and dive deep into [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon)'s Leadership Principles. The Hiring Manager focused on system design + leadership principles while others focused on coding + leadership principles.

❌ I did not make it this time. It was a bitter pill to swallow. I wanted it so bad, not just for me but also to help and motivate people close to me.

✅ It is what it is, things like this happen, we must not give up and have to keep going 💪. There are other opportunities out there waiting for us.

🙏 Big thanks to [Amazon](https://linkedin.com/company/amazon) and to everyone who supported me throughout this process. Big thanks to my Recruiter, who was kind enough to invest her time during prep calls.

🧑💻👩💻 And to everyone out there, keep learning something every day, stay active on [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/company/linkedin) by connecting, networking, posting content, liking and commenting on meaningful posts. Opportunities will come. I am optimistic and hopeful so should you, and I am not stopping here, neither should you.💪

## Summary

I recently interviewed for an SDE 2 position at Amazon, undergoing four rounds covering LLD, DSA, HLD, and a final Bar Raiser round with coding and leadership principles. While I performed well in some areas, the overall outcome of my loop is still uncertain.

## Full Experience

I recently completed my SDE 2 interview loop at Amazon, which consisted of four rounds.

#### Round 1 — LLD (Rate Limiter)

This round was focused on Low-Level Design (LLD) but also veered slightly into High-Level Design (HLD) aspects, where I discussed a Rate Limiter system. I also demonstrated strong leadership principles related to 'High standard and deliver result', leading to an 'Expected: Between Strong Hire / Hire' rating for this round.

#### Round 2 — DSA (Non-Bar Raiser)

The second round was a Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA) session. The problem involved designing a song recommendation system where a DJ plays the most frequent songs from a guest's list. I struggled a bit with finding the optimal solution in terms of complexity and speed. My leadership principles for this round focused on 'Bias of action and deep dive', resulting in a 'Lean Hire' expectation.

#### Round 3 — HLD (Aggregation System for Vending Machines)

The third round was dedicated to High-Level Design (HLD), where I tackled an Aggregation System for Vending Machines. I believe I showed good understanding after clarifications, proposed a correct data model, and logical aggregation. However, I missed some operational excellence considerations like retries, cron jobs, and Dead Letter Queues (DLQ). My leadership principles here were 'earn trust and ownership', and I was rated 'Expected: Lean Hire / Hire'.

#### Round 4 — Bar Raiser (Coding + LP)

Finally, the fourth round was with a Bar Raiser, combining both coding and leadership principles. I discussed leadership principles centered on 'customer obsession and new learning', for which I received a 'Strong Hire' expectation. The coding question required designing a data structure with`add(c)`,`remove(c)`,`getMaxChar()`, and`getMinChar()` functionalities. For this coding part, I was rated 'Expected: Between Hire/Lean Hire'. I'm currently waiting for the final decision and would be interested to hear from others in similar situations.

## Interview Questions (4)

1.

### Design a Rate Limiter

System Design

Design a Rate Limiter system. The discussion also touched upon High-Level Design (HLD) aspects.

2.

### Song Recommendation System

Data Structures & Algorithms

Guests provide a list of songs with their play counts. Design a system for a DJ to play songs that are most played by the guests. I struggled a bit with complexity and finding an optimal solution speed.

3.

### Design Aggregation System for Vending Machines

System Design

Design an aggregation system for vending machines. I considered data modeling and aggregation logic but also noted areas where I missed operational excellence aspects like retries, cron jobs, and Dead Letter Queues (DLQ).

4.

### Design Data Structure for Min/Max Char

Data Structures & Algorithms

Design a data structure that supports the following operations efficiently:

- `add(c)`: Add a character`c`.
- `remove(c)`: Remove a character`c`.
- `getMaxChar()`: Retrieve the character with the highest ASCII value.
- `getMinChar()`: Retrieve the character with the lowest ASCII value.

Amazon sde2 interview experience
I recently completed my interview loop for the SDE2 role at Amazon, and I wanted to share my experience for anyone preparing for similar roles.

🔹 Round 1 — Problem Solving & Coding
Problem: Design an index for file search.
Each file had a path and some text content (lowercase letters).
I had to implement:
⭐ insert(filePath, text)
⭐ vector find(word)
⭐ vector findWithPrefix(prefix)
I used a hybrid approach with a Trie + HashSet for fast lookup and prefix search.
↖️ Response: Extremely positive.

🔹 Round 2 — Low Level Design (LLD)
Problem: Design a vehicle rental service (initially for 2-wheelers but extensible to 4-wheelers).
We discussed:
⭐ Database schemas, API design, Applying Factory and Strategy patterns
⭐ Handling concurrency issues: preventing double bookings, avoiding double payments, ensuring consistent inventory updates
↖️ Response: Extremely positive.

🔹 Round 3 — High Level Design (HLD), done by hiring manager
Problem: Design a notification service supporting push, email, and SMS.
Key discussions:
⭐ Handling different message priorities (e.g., OTP as real-time high-priority)
⭐ Using message queues, topics/partitions, retry and backoff strategies
↙️ Response: Negative.

🔹 Round 4 — Bar Raiser
⭐ This round focused entirely on Leadership Principles.
The interviewer skipped the coding/problem-solving part, and we had a 45-minute scenario-based discussion.
➡️ Response: Neutral.

Final verdict: Rejected
But the learning definitely does not stop here.
Growing every day and looking forward to more challenges ahead.

Hi everyone,

After rescheduling around 10 times, I’ve finally completed my loop interviews with Amazon. I’m not entirely sure what to make of it since some rounds went extremely well, while in a few I messed up a little.

I’d love to hear from anyone with experience, what do you think my chances are?

Round 1: LLD + LP
LLD was about 7/10, and LP went really well - I’d rate it around 9.5/10, overall 8/10.

Round 2: DSA + LP
This round went very well. I solved the DSA question correctly within the time limit and handled the LP questions confidently. I’d rate it 9.5/10.

🚀 𝗕𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗗𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗠𝘆 𝗔𝗺𝗮𝘇𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝗗𝗘-𝟮 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀 (𝗟𝟱, 𝗕𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗲) 🚀

I completed my Amazon AWS SDE-2 (L5) interview process a while ago and wanted to share my experience to help others preparing for similar roles.

📘 Background
• Experience: ~6 years (4.5 yrs industry + 1.5 yrs upskilling)
• Education: B.Tech, Tier-3 College (2019 graduate)
• Last Role: Backend Developer at a Product-Based Company (~28 LPA)

🧩 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄 𝗧𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲
• ✅ Online Assessment: End of April
• 📞 Phone Screen: Early June → moved to final loop
• 🏢 Final Loop: 3 rounds on one day + Bar Raiser on the next

🔹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟭 – 𝗗𝗦𝗔
𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺: Rotten Oranges (Multi-source BFS)
• Implemented a full functional solution and discussed optimizations.
• Few questions on my previous experience and relevant tech.
𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀: Problem solving, code clarity, and LPs.

🔹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟮 – 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵-𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 (𝗛𝗟𝗗)
𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺: Design a News Feed System
• Discussed overall architecture, scalability, and data flow.
• Could have improved by simplifying data storage and selecting an appropriate DB for relationships.
𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀: Architecture, trade-offs, and LPs.

🔹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟯 – 𝗟𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 & 𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲
𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁: Simplified Splitwise-like system (minimize transactions among N people).
Proposed greedy approach using two max-heaps; later realized backtracking fits better (NP-Hard).
𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀: Problem structuring, maintainability, and LPs.

🔹 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟰 – 𝗕𝗮𝗿 𝗥𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗿
𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺: Design an API to respond under 2s latency for time-based queries (data in S3).
• Proposed stream-based processing with pre-aggregations stored in a time-series DB.
• Shifted aggregation to ingestion service for better query latency.
𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗔𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀: Scalability, latency handling, adaptability, and LPs.

💬 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆
This experience helped me understand Amazon’s expectations in design depth, coding structure, and decision reasoning.
It’s not just about knowing the right topics, but about how deeply you can reason through trade-offs. Hope this helps others calibrate their preparation better.
